press_release_title: How long do dental implants last? What to know
press_release_text: Anyone who has dealt with tooth loss knows that missing even a single tooth can affect your confidence and self-esteem, not to mention your diet. Fortunately, effective and long-lasting solutions exist. Dental implant restorations are a durable and long-lasting solution for replacing missing teeth. Designed to look and feel like natural teeth, they let you speak, eat, and smile like you did before tooth loss. Made from materials like titanium and zirconia, dental implants are built to last a lifetime. However, the quality of the restoration itself as well as your care and maintenance habits can influence its lifespan. If you’re wondering how dental implants work and how to make them last a long time, let’s explore the factors that influence their lifespan and how you can keep yours in top shape. What factors prolong the life of a dental implant? Your dental implants are an investment, so how do you make them last? Here’s what you need to know when considering dental implants near you : Choose high-quality materials A titanium implant bonds to your jawbone through a process called osseointegration. While titanium is a popular implant material in the market, zirconia is a ceramic alternative that offers strength and aesthetics. High-quality implants made of reliable materials may last longer. When it comes to dental implant crowns, zirconia is a strong option. Porcelain and ceramic offer slightly less durability but a natural look. Resin and acrylic crowns may be cheaper but more prone to wear and chipping. Maintain good oral hygiene Brushing your teeth and implants twice a day with a soft-bristled toothbrush can keep bacteria away. Use floss or a water flosser to clean around the implant as needed. Follow a diet low in sugar What you eat on a daily basis affects the life of your implants and surrounding tissues. A high-sugar diet can lead to plaque buildup, which may contribute to gum disease. Try a balanced diet with fewer processed foods (and less sugar) to help reduce the odds of plaque buildup and maintain good health. Get regular dental checkups Routine visits to your dentist are a key element of maintaining dental implants. Your dentist will check for signs of gum disease, implant wear, or bite misalignment. Catching potential issues early can prevent complications and prolong the life of your implant. Regular professional cleanings help remove plaque and bacteria that could compromise your implant’s stability. What factors can shorten the lifespan of dental implants? Here are some reasons why dental implants may fail, get damaged, or not last as long. Trauma or injury One wrong bite on ice or hard candy (or even an unexpected fall) can put your implant at risk. Too much force can loosen or potentially lead to implant failure. Protect your investment by wearing a mouthguard when playing sports. Smoking Studies show that smokers have a higher risk of dental implant failure than non-smokers. Nicotine can slow healing and raise the risk of infection, which is why dentists often advise quitting smoking. Allergy to titanium A sudden fall, an accidental hit, or even chewing on something too hard can harm your implant restoration. Too much pressure might loosen or damage it. To keep your smile secure, use a mouthguard during sports or while sleeping if you grind your teeth. Infection and gum disease Peri-implantitis is a condition similar to gum disease that affects dental implants. It occurs when bacteria accumulate around the implant, leading to inflammation and bone loss. Poor oral hygiene, smoking, or untreated gum disease can increase the risk of infection. Regular dental visits and proper oral care can prevent this issue. Bone loss Your dental implant needs a healthy jawbone for proper osseointegration. This helps the implant feel stable. Peri-implantitis, gum disease, or even osteoporosis can cause bone loss even after your implant has healed in place. Over time, bone loss in the jaw may weaken the support for an implant, causing it to become loose. Dental implant treatment can transform your smile, boost your confidence, and give you a new lease on life. But implant restorations need the right precautions and care to last a lifetime. Practicing good oral hygiene and getting regular checkups can go a long way toward helping your implants look and feel great for years. press_release_title: 7 Tips for a Motorcycle Trip
press_release_text: Riding a motorcycle on a long trip is an exciting adventure. Whether you’re cruising along coastal highways or winding through mountain roads, proper planning could make all the difference. Here are seven tips to ensure your motorcycle trip is smooth, safe and unforgettable: 1)Choose the right ride Your motorcycle should be well-suited for long-distance travel. Comfort, reliability, and fuel efficiency are important factors to consider. Touring bikes and cruisers are often preferred for their comfortable seats and smooth rides, while adventure bikes can better handle rougher terrain. No matter what type of bike you have, make sure it’s in top condition before you leave. Check the tires, brakes, fluids and lights to prevent any breakdowns on the road. If you’re considering upgrading to a more suitable bike or getting started with your first, a motorcycle loan can help make it more affordable. 2)Map out your trip Planning your route ahead of time can save you from unnecessary stress. Use GPS apps or a good old-fashioned map to chart where you’ll stop for fuel, food and rest. Consider scenic routes that offer breathtaking views and interesting landmarks. If you’re traveling in a group, communicate with your fellow riders about meeting points in case someone gets separated. 3)Prepare for all climates Weather can change quickly, especially when traveling through different regions. Dress in layers so you can adjust as needed. A waterproof jacket and gloves are helpful in case of rain, and breathable clothing will help you stay cool in the heat. Pack extra gear like thermal liners if you’re riding through colder areas. 4)Take the time to hydrate and refuel Long hours on a motorcycle can be exhausting, and dehydration can sneak up on you. Keep a water bottle handy and drink regularly, even if you don’t feel thirsty. Plan stops to stretch your legs and grab a meal. Fueling your body is just as important as fueling your bike. Speaking of fuel, make sure you don’t wait until the last minute to stop at a gas station—some routes may have long stretches without one 5)Have emergency tools handy A small tool kit could save you a lot of trouble if something goes wrong. Long road trips can wear down your bike—tires, parts and oil all need attention. Carry a basic tool kit for quick fixes, like a tire repair kit. Make sure the tools you get fit your bike. If you’re unsure, check if your motorcycle brand sells pre-made tool kits. Also, don’t forget to bring a first aid kit in case of minor injuries. 6)Stay willing to shift gears Even the best plans don’t always go as expected. Road closures, bad weather or mechanical issues may force you to make changes on the fly. Stay flexible and adapt to whatever comes your way. If you need to take a break or change your route, don’t hesitate. The goal of your trip is to enjoy the journey, not just reach the destination. Being open to new experiences could even make your adventure even more memorable. 7)Build up your riding stamina Riding for hours can be physically demanding, especially if you’re not used to it. Before heading out on a long trip, try taking shorter rides to build up your endurance. Practice riding for several hours at a time, with breaks in between, to get used to the feeling. Strengthening your core and legs with simple exercises may also help you stay comfortable on long rides. Capture every moment A motorcycle trip is an adventure worth remembering. Take pictures, record videos or even keep a travel journal to document your journey. If you’re riding with friends, share your experiences and create memories together. There are plenty of helmet cameras available that let you record your ride hands-free. Whether you post on social media or keep your memories private, looking back at your trip will bring back the thrill of the open road. So, get your bike ready, pack smart and hit the road for an unforgettable adventure! press_release_text: WASHINGTON DC, April 29, 2025 — The U.S. Minority Chamber of Commerce is pleased to invite the business community, particularly Honduran diaspora leaders residing in New Orleans, to participate in the Honduras Convention for Real Estate Investment, Projects, and Business Opportunities New Orleans 2025. The event will take place from July 10-13 at the Chamber’s convention center in New Orleans. The convention is open to the public and requires advance registration. Honduras: A Land of Untapped Potential With 15 years of established operations in Honduras, the U.S. Minority Chamber of Commerce brings unparalleled expertise and connections to this investment initiative. Honduras represents one of Central America’s most promising investment landscapes, offering diverse opportunities across multiple sectors at competitive price points compared to neighboring countries. The mission of the event is to showcase Honduras as a unique destination for buying, developing, expanding, and exploiting economic development opportunities through investments in hotels-motels, restaurants, supermarkets, land, farms, housing construction, industrial parks, and more. The convention particularly targets the Honduran diaspora in New Orleans, a city often referred to as the “Catracha Capital” in the United States. Among the showcase opportunities are beachfront residential complexes and small islands ideal for retirement or tourism investment ventures. Honduras’ 430-mile Caribbean coastline, alongside its Pacific shores, offers pristine beaches and development potential at prices significantly lower than comparable locations in Mexico or Costa Rica. press_release_title: 4 Ways to Pick a Credit Monitoring Service
press_release_text: As of 2023, Federal Trade Commission data reported that consumers lost over $10 billion due to identity theft and fraud. And even if you’ve been lucky enough to evade identity theft thus far, just like you’d keep an eye on your home security, there’s nothing wrong with protecting your credit – which is why credit monitoring is a must in the digital age. Credit monitoring is a service that continuously tracks your credit reports from the major credit bureaus for any changes, self-imposed or otherwise. This includes any new accounts opened in your name, hard inquiries from lenders, and changes to your personal information. By regularly checking your credit reports and alerting you to any suspicious activity, credit monitoring services allow for early detection of potential identity theft or fraud. But with so many services available, how do you know which is the best one to pick? Read on to find out the best tips and tricks for picking the perfect credit monitoring service. 4 Ways to Pick a Credit Monitoring Service 1. Choose Based on Features If you’re looking for a specific service offered by a credit monitoring service, you’ll want to weigh your decisions based heavily using that service. A good credit monitoring system includes all three major bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion). Also, ask yourself whether or not you’d like a service that offers only your FICO ® Score or other score models as well. Also, you could look for services that offer dark web monitoring, fraud alerts, data breach monitoring, or credit freeze assistance. Other features of credit monitoring services include credit simulations, which allows you to see how different actions might affect your score. If credit repair assistance is one of your must-haves, be careful – credit repair scams are everywhere, and you don’t want to be subject to one of them. 2. Choose Based on Pricing and Plans It’s rare you’ll find a free credit monitoring plan that retains legitimacy and provides a decent service. For the most part, you’ll have to pay a subscription fee. As such, you’ll want to compare monthly and annual subscription fees based on how much it’ll save you. If you do find a free service, analyze the pros and cons of what the free product offers versus a paid product. Ask yourself, are free trials available? And does the company offer any guarantees? 3.Choose Based on Customer Service and Support In case you need help with your credit monitoring service, you’ll want to know how easily it is to you contact customer support through either phone, email, or a chat service. How quickly do they typically respond to inquiries? To get a sense of this, read reviews from other customers to gauge their experiences. 4.Choose Based on Company Reputation and Security When credit reports can be subject to dangers such as identity theft, you’ll want a safe service that can guarantee protection. Ask yourself, how does the company protect your personal information? Is the company reputable and well-established? Check the company’s rating with the Better Business Bureau to see if their security is to your personal standards. Choosing the Right Service for You Everyone’s needs are different, so before you pick your preferred credit monitoring service, check in with yourself to assess your needs. What level of credit monitoring and identity theft protection you need, your budget, and your priorities, such as comprehensive features, low cost, and excellent customer service. You could even go so far as to create a comparison chart to easily measure features, pricing, and customer reviews of different services. No matter what, your credit is worth the cost of protection. If you don’t want to compromise on cost, features, or safety, look into a service like MyFICO ® that can start you on the road back to credit-consciousness. press_release_title: Paradigm Asset Management Launches PaaS Invest: A New Portfolio-as-a-Service Platform Merging Direct Indexing and Dynamic Active Management
press_release_text: New York, NY, April 30, 2025 —New York, NY, May 1, 2025 — Paradigm Asset Management, led by CEO James Francis — a pioneer in data-driven investment strategies for more than three decades — today announced the launch of PaaS Invest, a next-generation Portfolio as a Service (PaaS) platform set to transform wealth management. PaaS Invest sits at the convergence of advanced AI, deep market data, and seasoned human insight, delivering Total Portfolio Personalization. The platform seamlessly integrates the precision of Direct Indexing with the dynamic flexibility of active management, empowering investors to achieve tailored, adaptive portfolios at scale. Rooted in years of experience providing sophisticated investment solutions to institutional clients, Paradigm recognized that the recent surge in demand for AI-powered and customizable portfolio strategies made now the ideal moment to expand its offering. With PaaS Invest, Paradigm is formally opening its platform to a broader market of wealth advisors, family offices, and institutional investors seeking cutting-edge, scalable, and tax-efficient solutions. “PaaS Invest is the natural evolution of what we’ve been building at Paradigm for years,” said James Francis, CEO of Paradigm Asset Management. “As the industry embraces AI and personalization, we are proud to deliver a platform that brings the full power of institutional-quality strategies, advanced data analytics, and ease of use directly to advisors and institutions.” The Future of Investing: Total Portfolio Personalization PaaS Invest enables wealth managers to create truly customized portfolios — not just mirror indices — by offering: Direct Indexing Precision: Tailor portfolios to align with client-specific ESG preferences, tax strategies, and risk profiles. Dynamic Active Management: Powered by Dynamic Collective Intelligence (DCI) and the Collective Intelligence Portfolio Engine (CIPE), portfolios adapt in real-time to changing market conditions. Seamless User Experience: Built for speed, simplicity, and transparency, the platform allows advisors to manage complex strategies without complexity. Unlike static or “one-size-fits-all” solutions, PaaS Invest empowers users to overlay tax optimization and personalized constraints not only on passive portfolios but also on active, data-driven strategies — a first-of-its-kind offering. “Today’s clients expect more than just investment products — they expect personalization, transparency, and performance,” said Gregory Pai, Senior Managing Director at Paradigm Asset Management. “PaaS Invest gives advisors and institutions the ability to deliver all three, with an elegant, tech-enabled solution that evolves alongside their clients’ needs.” Bringing Institutional Power to a Broader Market Paradigm Asset Management has long been known for harnessing data and research to build sophisticated investment solutions for institutional investors. With PaaS Invest, the firm is making those capabilities more accessible — bringing institutional-grade insights, customization, and adaptability to a wider audience without sacrificing rigor or performance standards. The launch underscores Paradigm’s belief that the future of wealth management lies at the convergence of personalization, AI-driven intelligence, and human expertise — and that advisors and investors need tools that are as dynamic as the markets they navigate. Availability and Next Steps PaaS Invest is currently available to select early adopters and will roll out to a broader market over the coming months. Wealth advisors, family offices, and institutional investors interested in learning more can: Visit: www.paasinvest.com Request a Demo: Schedule a personalized consultation with a member of the PaaS Invest team. press_release_title: How to Keep Kids Safe Around the Pool
press_release_text: A swimming pool is a great way for families to have fun, stay active and cool off on hot days. But pools can also be dangerous, especially for children. Drowning is one of the leading causes of death for young kids so pool safety should always be a top priority. Whether you got a pool loan to build your backyard pool or visit a community one, there are steps you can take to keep kids safe. Let’s explore important safety tips to help you protect children around the pool: Take swimming lessons One of the most effective ways to keep kids safe around the pool is by teaching them how to swim. Swimming lessons can help children gain confidence in the water and learn essential skills such as floating, treading water and basic strokes. Learning how to stay afloat in deep water and knowing how to exit the pool safely could make a big difference in preventing accidents. Install proper barriers and safety equipment A fence that is at least four feet high with a self-latching gate could help keep young children from wandering into the pool area. If possible, install an alarm on the gate to alert you if it’s opened. Always have adult supervision Children should never be left alone near a pool, even for a short time. An adult should always be watching when kids are swimming or playing near the water. Avoid distractions like texting or reading while supervising. Young children and inexperienced swimmers should stay within arm’s reach of an adult. If you have guests over, designate a responsible adult as the “water watcher.” This person should focus only on monitoring the kids in the pool to prevent accidents. Use life jackets for safety Life jackets provide extra safety for young children or kids who are not strong swimmers. Make sure the life jacket fits properly and is approved by the U.S. Coast Guard. Even with a life jacket, kids should still be supervised at all times when in or near the water. Keep pool areas free of hazards Slippery pool decks can lead to falls and injuries. To reduce the risk, keep pool areas dry and free of toys, towels and other items that could cause someone to trip. Non-slip mats and poolside safety signs can also help prevent accidents. Learn CPR and emergency procedures Even with safety precautions, accidents can happen. Knowing CPR could save a child’s life in an emergency. Many local organizations, including the American Red Cross, offer CPR training classes. Along with CPR, have a plan in place for emergencies. Keep a phone nearby to call 911 if needed and post emergency numbers in a visible spot. Make sure babysitters or caregivers know what to do in case of an accident. Educate children about the risks Kids need to understand that pools can be dangerous if they are not careful. Have age-appropriate conversations about why safety rules are important. Explain that running near the pool, rough play or pushing others in the water could lead to accidents. Set clear rules for pool use Establish rules for pool time and make sure everyone follows them. Some important rules include: No swimming without an adult present. No diving in shallow areas. No rough play or pushing others into the water. No running near the pool. The importance of pool safety Keeping kids safe around the pool requires constant attention and preparation. By having pool safety measures in place you may ensure that your pool remains a fun and secure place for your family. With the right precautions, you can enjoy peace of mind while your kids have fun in the water. press_release_text: ASC Advisors Joins as Exclusive Communications Partner to PBHFA Palm Beach, Florida – May 1, 2025 – The Palm Beach Hedge Fund Association (“PBHFA”) is pleased to welcome ASC Advisors (“ASC”), a strategic communications firm focused on the alternative investment management industry, as a new member of the PBHFA and as its exclusive communications partner. “I am thrilled to welcome ASC Advisors into the PBHFA community as it expands its presence in South Florida! Given its specialized focus and long history in advising alternative managers on communications initiatives, the firm is the optimal fit for our membership & network of hedge funds, private equity partnerships and alternative investment firms. I look forward to sharing their insights, capabilities and services with our group and working more closely with them moving forward,” said David Goodboy, Founder of The Palm Beach Hedge Fund Association. ASC has long-standing roots in hedge fund and alternative investment communications stretching back over 30 years. Partnering with the PBHFA represents another key milestone in ASC’s ongoing commitment to strengthening its presence in the South Florida market, where it continues to advise leading investment managers, attract top-talent, and pursue opportunities to enhance the firm’s overall capabilities, expertise, and ability to deliver communications strategy for existing and prospective clients. The partnership with PBHFA follows the recent hiring of Max Rayden as Senior Director in West Palm Beach. A senior communications advisor with significant experience working with investment managers across media relations, brand building, reputation management, special situations, M&A transactions, and crisis communications, Max joined Miami-based ASC Managing Director and communications veteran Keely Gispan as a senior ASC team member in South Florida. “We are thrilled to work with The PBHFA as exclusive communications partner. David and the Association have built a truly unique community of alternative investment managers that reflects the strength of Palm Beach and wider South Florida as a vibrant, innovative, and attractive financial ecosystem,” said Max Rayden, Senior Director at ASC Advisors. About ASC Advisors ASC Advisors is a strategic communications firm that supports leading hedge funds, private equity, credit/private credit, venture capital, real estate, crypto and other investment management firms. As the largest team in the communications industry dedicated exclusively to alternative investment management, we partner with managers throughout market cycles and various stages of their evolution. ASC’s exclusive focus on alternative investment management enables the Firm to offer a wide range of capabilities, including public, media and investor relations, shareholder activism and M&A, special situations and crisis support. For more information, visit www.ascadvisors.com . Its members consist of active hedge fund managers/ professionals, ultra-high net worth investors, private equity firms, venture capitalists, family offices, financial traders, investment bankers, academics, financial institutions, FOF’s, foundations, allocators, as well as the world’s leading financial service providers. press_release_title: Avoid These Foods to Protect Your Teeth and Gums
press_release_text: Taking care of your teeth and gums is a big part of staying healthy. Brushing and flossing are very important, but the food you eat also matters. Some foods can harm your teeth and gums if you’re not careful. These foods can cause cavities, gum problems and even make your breath smell bad. Fixing these issues can get expensive, so some people look into dental financing to help pay for care. Let’s look at the top foods to avoid (or eat less of) to keep your smile strong and healthy: Sticky candy Candy that sticks to your teeth — like taffy, caramel or gummy bears — can be really bad for your mouth. These sweet treats stay on your teeth for a long time. The sugar feeds the bacteria in your mouth, which then creates acid. That acid wears down the enamel (the hard outer layer of your teeth), leading to cavities. If you do eat sticky candy, try to brush your teeth soon after or rinse your mouth with water. Interestingly, the American Dental Association notes that chocolate tends to rinse off teeth more easily than other types of candy. Dark chocolate with at least 70% cacao may even offer some potential health benefits—making it a slightly better treat for your smile. Carbonated drinks Soda is full of sugar, and even diet soda contains acid. Both types can hurt your teeth. The acid in soda breaks down enamel, and the sugar helps bacteria grow. Try switching to water or unsweetened drinks. If you still want soda now and then, drink it through a straw to keep it away from your teeth. When you sip soda throughout the day, your teeth get covered in acid again and again. Soda also dries out your mouth, so you have less saliva, and dark sodas can leave stains or discolor your teeth. Keep in mind — don’t brush your teeth right after drinking soda because doing that can actually speed up tooth damage. Coffee and tea Drinking coffee or tea every day can stain your teeth. If you add sugar or flavored syrups, it’s even worse. Like soda, hot drinks can be sipped slowly, giving bacteria more time to grow. Citrus fruits Fruits like lemons, limes, oranges and grapefruits are healthy in many ways but are also very acidic. That acid can wear down enamel and make your teeth more sensitive. If you have sores in your mouth, citrus fruits might also make them worse. You don’t have to stop eating citrus fruits altogether. After eating them, just rinse your mouth with water. Ice Chewing ice might seem harmless, but biting on ice cubes can crack, chip or break your teeth. You can still enjoy a cold drink or suck on ice but don’t bite down on it. Chips and crackers Starchy snacks like chips and crackers might not seem sugary, but they turn into sugar once they’re in your mouth. These foods can get stuck between your teeth and gums, which gives bacteria time to grow. Dried fruit Dried fruits like raisins, apricots and cranberries are often seen as healthy snacks. But they are sticky and full of natural sugar. Just like candy, they cling to your teeth and feed bacteria. Popcorn Popcorn itself isn’t too bad for your teeth, but unpopped kernels can crack your teeth if you bite down on one. Also, popcorn husks can get stuck in your gums, causing pain and even infection if not removed.Chew carefully and floss after eating popcorn to avoid problems. Keep your smile safe Protecting your teeth and gums is easier when you’re mindful about what you eat. A healthy mouth helps you feel better, look better, and enjoy your favorite foods without pain or problems. Taking care of your teeth now can also help you avoid bigger dental problems in the future. That means fewer visits to the dentist for fillings, gum treatments or other costly procedures. Your smile is one of the first things people notice, so keeping it bright and healthy is probably worth the effort. Start by checking what’s in your pantry and swapping out harmful snacks for tooth-friendly options. The little things you do today could help your teeth stay strong for years to come. press_release_title: Pros and Cons of Adding a Pool to Your Backyard
press_release_text: Adding a swimming pool to your backyard could be a big decision. It can bring lots of fun, increase your home’s value and provide a great way to cool off in the summer. However, it also comes with costs, maintenance and responsibilities. Some homeowners look into pool loans to help cover the cost, but is a pool even the right choice for you? Before jumping into this investment, it’s important to weigh the pros and cons. Pros of adding a pool Increases home value A well-maintained pool can make your home more attractive to potential buyers. Many people see a pool as a luxury feature and may be willing to pay more for a home that has one. In warmer climates, especially, having a pool could be a major selling point. Great for exercise Swimming is a fantastic workout. It’s easy on the joints and great for building strength and endurance. If you’re looking for a way to stay fit without going to the gym, having a pool in your backyard could be the right alternative. Perfect for family fun and entertaining A pool creates a fun space for family and friends to gather. Whether it’s hosting pool parties, playing games with the kids or simply relaxing by the water, a pool can bring people together. It can also keep kids entertained during the summer months. Offers a relaxing escape There’s something peaceful about lounging by the pool on a sunny day with a delicious beverage. The sound of water, the fresh air and the ability to take a dip whenever you want can create a vacation-like atmosphere in your own backyard. Can improve mental health Spending time in the water can reduce stress and anxiety. Swimming has been linked to improved mood and better sleep. A pool provides a space to unwind after a long day and enjoy the benefits of being outdoors. Cons of adding a pool High initial cost Pools are expensive to install. The price can vary depending on the type and size, but homeowners often spend thousands of dollars on construction. Ongoing maintenance Owning a pool requires regular upkeep. You’ll need to clean it, check chemical levels and possibly hire a professional for maintenance. Pool filters, pumps and heaters may also need repairs or replacements over time, adding to the cost. Higher utility bills A pool can increase your water and electricity bills. You’ll need water to fill and maintain the pool and running the pump and heater can add to your energy costs. You could expect even higher expenses if you live in a cooler climate and want to heat your pool. Potential safety risks Pools can be dangerous, especially for young children and pets. Drowning is a serious risk and safety measures like fences, covers and alarms are essential. If you have kids, you’ll need to be extra cautious and always supervise them around the pool. May not add enough value to justify the cost While pools can make a home more attractive, they don’t always increase home value enough to cover the installation cost. In some areas, like where it’s cold most of the year, buyers may see a pool as a hassle rather than a benefit. If you’re adding a pool mainly as an investment, make sure it makes sense for your local market. Weigh the pros and cons Adding a pool to your backyard can be a big decision that comes with both advantages and challenges. While a pool can enhance your home’s value, provide endless entertainment and create a personal oasis, it also requires significant maintenance, upfront costs and potential safety concerns. Whether you decide to take the plunge or explore other backyard upgrades, making an informed choice ensures you’ll enjoy your outdoor space to the fullest. press_release_title: Financial Planning in Your 40s: 5 Tips for Money Management
press_release_text: Many people begin to approach their peak earning years in their 40s and may start to feel more financially settled. However, responsibilities often increase during this time as well. With children preparing for college, retirement getting closer, and possibly aging parents to care for, it’s essential to adopt the right strategies to stay on track or even get ahead. This article explores five tips to improve your money management in your 40s. Manage lifestyle inflation As your income increases in your 40s, so might your spending, a phenomenon known as lifestyle inflation. While there’s nothing inherently wrong with rewarding yourself, it’s important to control this inflation. Some people increase their spending in line with or even beyond their income, which can hinder their financial goals and lead to strain. Ensure that you cover all essential bills and meet your savings targets first. Then, evaluate how much discretionary income you have left. You can use this extra for enjoyable purchases like vacations or saving for a nicer vehicle. Check your emergency fund Emergency funds are meant to cover three to six months of living expenses. If your income and expenses have increased, your emergency fund may need an update as well. Review your fund and prioritize saving more until you reach that three to six-month range again. If you have children, consider aiming for the higher end of the range, as having more people in the household can increase the likelihood of unexpected expenses. Additionally, review your savings account to see if you can find one with a higher interest rate to help your emergency fund grow faster and keep up with inflation. Evaluate your insurance coverage Your insurance needs can change over time, and your 40s are an ideal time to reassess your policies. You may need to adjust coverage or explore ways to reduce costs. For example, if you have children nearing the age of 26, they may soon need to obtain their own health insurance. This could allow you to remove them from your plan or switch to a more cost-effective option. Other policies to evaluate include: Life insurance is particularly crucial since it helps protects your family. Many start by comparing term vs. permanent life insurance . Term life insurance is competitively priced but only lasts for a specified period, such as 10, 20, or 30 years, and lacks a wealth-building component. This causes some to wonder, “ What is permanent life insurance ?” when exploring their options. Permanent life insurance is generally less competitive, but it typically lasts for life and offers a cash value growth component to help you build wealth as you pay premiums. It may be more suitable if you’re considering life insurance as part of your estate planning or need to help protect loved ones for a longer period. Explore additional ways to save and invest While retirement accounts may be the cornerstone of your savings, higher income in your 40s may bring you closer to contribution limits. This is a good time to explore other savings and investment options. For instance, a taxable brokerage account is a solid way to invest more. While these accounts don’t offer pre-tax deductions or tax-free withdrawals, they allow you to withdraw funds at any time. Holding assets for more than a year before selling can also qualify you for lower long-term capital gains tax rates. These features make taxable brokerage accounts an excellent option for those considering early retirement or saving for other goals. Another option is the cash value component of permanent life insurance, which grows tax-deferred at a rate that varies by policy type. Eventually, you can withdraw from or borrow against it. Revisit your investment allocation Although retirement may still be a couple of decades away, it’s closer than before. If you’ve consistently saved in your retirement accounts, you likely have a substantial balance by now. Your 40s are a good time to revisit your investment allocation to ensure your assets are performing as needed and make adjustments if necessary. For example, you may want to shift your retirement account allocation toward more conservative or income-producing investments. Meanwhile, you might consider using more aggressive investments in your taxable accounts to minimize potential dividend-related taxes and balance stability with growth potential. Working with a financial advisor can help. They can review your allocation and investment performance, then develop a plan to reallocate assets if needed. The bottom line By their 40s, many people start to feel more financially stable, making it harder to determine their next financial moves. Focus on managing lifestyle inflation, replenishing your emergency fund, and evaluating your insurance coverage. Then, seek additional ways to save and invest, but revisit your investment allocation before making any moves. Consulting with a financial advisor is wise. They can help you outline your situation and goals, and then work with you to create a plan that can help to move you toward those goals. press_release_title: 5 risks after getting dental implant surgery
press_release_text: Broken or missing teeth can make day-to-day tasks like eating your favorite foods and public speaking a challenge. Dental implants in Greenville offer a reliable, long-lasting option to help restore your ability to chew and speak and repair the look of your smile. If you’re considering a dental implant operation to reconstruct your teeth, you may be curious about how the process works and the risks involved. The dental implant process How long do dental implants take? This varies depending on how many implants are being placed and the complexity of the procedure. The surgery can typically be finished in a single office visit that lasts between one and two hours. The reason the dental implant process takes several months is because of the time it takes to heal after the procedure before having a permanent prosthesis placed. Here are the steps involved in a single tooth dental implant procedure: Your prosthodontist will make a small incision and insert a titanium implant below the surface of the gums into the jawbone. The titanium fuses with the bone during a process called osseointegration, which forms an artificial root system and a stable foundation for the new teeth. Once the implant post is healed, the dentist will attach an abutment, which will connect a crown, or artificial tooth, to the implant. Your dentist will place a custom-made crown that matches the color, size, and shape of your existing teeth onto the abutment. What are the risks of dental implant surgery? Dental implant surgery has become a common solution to replace missing or damaged teeth. There are different types of dental implants available, and your dentist can help you decide which option suits your dental goals. As with any surgical procedure, there are potential complications of dental implant surgery. Before you proceed with the operation, familiarize yourself with some of the risks. 1. Implant failure Dental implants have a high success rate. But, if a dental implant doesn’t heal properly or the titanium doesn’t fuse correctly with the jawbone, it can become unstable. If you notice that the implant has shifted or you feel pain when chewing or speaking at the implant site after the allotted recovery time, you may need to replace the dental implant. Fortunately, the dental implant replacement process is straightforward. Talk to your dentist about the options. 2. Infection As with any open wound, bacteria that find their way into the implant site can lead to infections, like peri-implantitis, and cause tenderness, swelling, and pus. Follow your oral surgeon’s instructions to lessen your risk of infection and promote healthy implant healing. Practicing good oral hygiene habits can also minimize your risk of infection. Brush twice daily with a soft-bristled toothbrush and non-abrasive toothpaste, floss, and rinse with antimicrobial mouthwash to remove food particles and bacteria. 3. Nerve and tissue damage After dental implant surgery, the surrounding area may feel numb or tingly from the anesthesia, but normal sensation should return within a few days after the operation. If the numbness or tingling persists or if you feel pain in your face, chin, or lips, it could mean that the implant was improperly placed. Visit your dentist right away to address your concerns. 4. Swelling, pain, and minor bleeding After dental implant surgery, side effects like redness, swelling, pain, and some bleeding are typical. A cold compress could minimize swelling and inflammation post-surgery, over-the-counter pain relievers may help to manage the discomfort, and gently applying gauze to the site can help curtail bleeding. If any of these symptoms persist for longer than a few days or the prescribed recovery period outlined by your dentist, give them a call. 5. Gum recession Gum recession can sometimes occur after getting dental implants, leading to exposed roots as the gums pull away from the teeth. Discuss signs of gum recession with your dentist before the condition worsens to minimize your risk of infection and implant failure. The bottom line Dental implants are a reliable solution for replacing cracked or missing teeth, but the surgery isn’t without its risks. Understanding the potential complications and risks following your implant surgery can set you up for success in the days and weeks following the procedure. press_release_title: 8 Tips to Improve Your Teeth and Avoid a Trip to the Dentist
press_release_text: Going to the dentist isn’t always fun. While regular checkups are essential for maintaining oral health, it’s much better to prevent issues like cavities, toothaches or root canals before they start. Not only can dental problems be painful, but they can also get expensive. That’s why many people look into dental financing to help cover the cost of care. But wouldn’t it be better to at least try and avoid the problem in the first place? Here are eight easy tips to help keep your teeth healthy and strong so you can avoid extra trips to the dentist. 1)Brush your teeth twice a day Brushing your teeth is the most basic step — but also the most important! Brushing your teeth in the morning and at night removes food and plaque that build up throughout the day. Plaque is a sticky film of bacteria that can cause cavities and gum disease if you don’t clean it away. Use a soft-bristled toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste. Brush for two full minutes, cleaning all sides of your teeth — front, back and chewing surfaces. 2)Floss daily Flossing might seem annoying, but it’s super helpful. Your toothbrush can’t reach between your teeth, and that’s where leftover food and bacteria love to hide. Flossing once a day removes that gunk and keeps your gums healthy.If you don’t like regular floss, try floss picks or a water flosser. Just make sure you’re cleaning between every tooth. 3)Cut back on sugar We all love sweet treats — candy, soda, cookies — but sugar is your teeth’s worst enemy. When sugar sits on your teeth, it feeds the bacteria that cause cavities. The more sugar you eat, the more likely you’ll end up with a painful problem.Try to limit sugary snacks and drinks. Drink water instead of soda and brush your teeth after eating sweets when you can. 4)Chew sugar-free gum Chewing sugar-free gum after meals helps your mouth produce more saliva. Saliva helps clean teeth and neutralize acids that can wear down enamel. Look for gum that has the American Dental Association (ADA) seal on the package. That means it’s been tested and proven to help your teeth. 5)Use antibacterial mouthwash Antibacterial mouthwash helps to fight harmful germs in your mouth. It not only washes away food and debris but also helps reduce plaque on your teeth. Make sure to pick a mouthwash without alcohol to avoid making your mouth feel dry. 6)Eat healthy food that’s good for your teeth Foods like milk and dairy products, apples, cranberries, tea and other high-fiber foods are great for your teeth. They’re full of vitamins and minerals.Plus, they help you make more saliva, which is great for your mouth. 7)Don’t use your teeth as tools It might be tempting to open a bag of chips or tear off a clothing tag with your teeth — but don’t do it. Using your teeth as tools can cause them to chip, crack or wear down faster. Always use scissors or the right tool for the job. You should only use your teeth for chewing food! 8)Visit the dentist regularly (even if you feel fine) Yes, the goal is to avoid extra trips to the dentist — but you still need regular checkups. Dentists can spot small problems before they turn into big ones. A quick cleaning and exam every six months could help keep your teeth in tip-top shape. Healthy habits today, fewer dental visits tomorrow Taking care of your teeth isn’t just about avoiding problems — it’s about staying healthy and feeling good. Your teeth help you talk, smile and feel confident. Taking care of them doesn’t have to be hard — it just takes doing the right things every day. press_release_title: Your Credit Score’s Impact on the Mortgage Process
press_release_text: Worried your credit score isn’t high enough to qualify for a mortgage? Knowing which credit score mortgage lenders use may help clarify what kind of offers and loan options could be available. But with multiple scoring models in use, figuring out which scores lenders rely on can be confusing. The good news: identifying the right credit score isn’t the only key. Understanding how scoring models work and what lenders value most can simplify your credit goals. Read on to learn which scores matter, how scoring models work and some tips to secure a more affordable mortgage. Why do credit scores matter for mortgages? Credit scores, a numerical representation of a person’s creditworthiness based on their credit history, can play a starring role in the mortgage application process. Why? Two government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs), Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, guarantee most mortgages in the U.S. A GSE guarantee reduces lender risks, making mortgages more affordable and accessible. Loans that don’t meet GSE standards are often more expensive. To qualify for a GSE-backed mortgage, you usually need to have a credit score of at least 620. So, your credit score isn’t just a number. It can also be a path to an affordable 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. For loan programs that involve higher risk like lower down payments or higher debt-to-income (DTI) ratios, the minimum score may need to be higher (more in the 660 to 680 range.) However, the exact score requirement can depend on the lender and loan program. Which credit score do mortgage lenders use? Nearly all top U.S. lenders use FICO ® Scores. Lenders grab the scores from the three main credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian and TransUnion) and may zero in on your middle score – or the second highest of the three. If you’re applying with a partner, they might use their second highest score if it’s lower. The FICO ® Score 8 is the score generally used for lending decisions by banks, but mortgage lenders primarily use FICO ® Score 2, FICO ® Score 5, and FICO ® Score 4. If you are applying with a co-signer, both individual’s FICO ® Scores will be pulled, and the lender will determine the median score for both applicants. They will use the lower of those two. What about credit scoring models? The Classic FICO® scoring model is the standard currently. A new scoring model that factors in rent and utility payments called the FICO ® Score 10T was proposed and approved by The Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA), but as of January implementation has been delayed for the foreseeable future. New models may be introduced but the FICO ® Score remains the primary one used by lenders. Do credit checks hurt your score? Usually, when you check your own credit, it’s a freebie – no impact! But when lenders check, it is considered a hard inquiry and can bring your score down slightly (around 5 points or less and the drop is temporary). The cool part? Multiple credit checks for the same type of loan within (typically 14 to 45 days) won’t dent your score as they are treated as a single inquiry. You can explore your options confidently during that time window. Should you avoid other loans before getting a mortgage? Yes. Car loans or credit card applications can temporarily lower your score, making lenders more cautious as they review your credit history. Keeping your credit profile free of recent applications shows lenders you’re financially steady and ready for a mortgage. Save new credit applications until after your mortgage approval to keep your score in top shape. How can you improve your credit score for a mortgage? Improving your credit score doesn’t have to be a mystery. Here are four simple strategies to boost your numbers and impress lenders: Pay your bills on time, even the minimums. Keep your balances low and your credit limit high. Stick with older accounts for a solid history. Mix it up over time. Credit cards, car loans and student loans can add variety. These consistent, responsible credit behaviors can give your score the boost it needs to secure a mortgage you’re proud of. Mortgage lenders may look beyond your credit score Though your credit score is of the utmost importance to lenders they take other factors into account. Lenders will consider income, collateral and DTI amongst others. Keeping your financial health intact by regularly reviewing your credit report and paying off any outstanding debts will help ensure your chances are as strong as possible when you apply for a mortgage. press_release_title: How to Jumpstart Your Savings in 2025
press_release_text: Saving money isn’t always easy — especially when everything seems to cost more these days. But whether you’re prepping for an emergency or working toward a big goal, having some savings set aside can give you serious peace of mind. If you’re ready to make 2025 the year you take control of your finances, here are a few simple ways to kickstart your savings journey. Create a budget Before you can start saving, you need to know where your money is actually going. Start by tracking your spending for a month or two to help you spot areas where you might be able to cut back. You don’t need to overhaul your entire lifestyle overnight. Even small changes can add up to big savings over time. Once you’ve built a budget that works for you, try your best to stick with it (but give yourself some grace if things don’t go perfectly right away). There’s no one-size-fits-all method for budgeting, but here are a few tried-and-true methods you can try: The 50/30/20 rule This method divides your after-tax income into three categories: 50% for needs (like housing, groceries, and utilities) 30% for wants (such as dining out or entertainment) 20% for savings and debt repayment It’s a helpful way to balance your spending and ensure that saving is part of your plan. The envelope system With the envelope system, you set a spending limit for each category — like groceries or gas — and place that amount in a labeled envelope. When the envelope is empty, you pause spending in that category until the next budget cycle. For example, if you have $500 to spend on groceries for the month, you would put $500 in an envelope marked “groceries.” Once the money in the envelope is gone, you cannot spend any more in that category until the next month. If something comes up and you need to spend more than what’s in an envelope, you can reallocate funds from another category — but do it with intent. For example, if you overspend on groceries, you might take money from your dining out envelope to cover the difference. This helps you stay within your overall budget while adjusting to real-life needs. Zero-based budgeting Zero-based budgeting gives every dollar of your income a specific purpose, so by the time you’re done planning, your income minus your expenses equals zero. That doesn’t mean you spend all your money — it just means you’re making sure your money goes exactly where you need it to, including savings, debt payments, and entertainment. At the beginning of each month, list all your expected income, then plan out your expenses down to the last dollar. That includes everything — rent, groceries, transportation, subscriptions, savings contributions, and even a little wiggle room for unexpected costs. If you earn $3,000 in a month, every dollar of that $3,000 should be assigned somewhere in your budget. Figure out what you want to save for Before you set savings goals, take a moment to define why you want to save. Are you building a rainy-day fund? Planning for a down payment on a home? Saving for retirement or a dream vacation? Having a purpose behind your savings makes it easier to stay focused and motivated. Set goals Once you know what you’re saving for, it’s time to set targets. Break your goal into manageable pieces –– how much do you need to save each month to reach it in a year? In three years? Setting clear, realistic goals gives your budget direction and helps you measure progress. Automate your savings One of the best ways to jumpstart your savings is to automate! Have a certain amount of money automatically transferred from your checking account into your savings account each month. This way, you’ll never even see the money, and you’ll be less likely to spend it. Cut out unnecessary expenses Take a close look at your spending habits. Are there any subscriptions you don’t use? Could you cut back on takeout or impulse shopping? You don’t have to give up everything you enjoy—just look for areas where you can spend less without feeling deprived. Even saving $50 or $100 a month can make a big difference over time. 6. Use financial tools wisely In some cases, emergency loans can help you manage short-term financial setbacks, like medical bills or urgent car repairs. But they shouldn’t be your go-to for building savings. If you do take out a loan, use it strategically: pay off high-interest debt, then focus on rebuilding your savings so you’re better prepared next time. Always borrow responsibly and understand the terms before committing. Bottom line There’s no time like the present to start saving for your future. Whether you’re just beginning your savings journey or looking to level up your habits in 2025, the key is consistency. With the right mindset, tools, and goals in place, you can make real progress toward financial peace of mind. press_release_title: How to maximize the lifespan of implant dentures
press_release_text: If you have missing or broken teeth, dental implant treatment can make a big difference in your day-to-day life. Dental implants can restore your ability to eat and speak, minimize discomfort, and even help you feel more confident. When searching for dental implants near you , you may consider implant dentures. These reliable and long-lasting tooth replacement options work well for many individuals. Whether you have implant dentures , zygomatic implants, or implant-supported bridges, proper care can help you maintain your artificial teeth, preserve your oral hygiene, and boost your self-esteem. Let’s review the top ways to keep implant dentures in excellent condition. Practice good oral hygiene Protecting your implant dentures means practicing good oral care habits. Brush at least twice daily with a gentle brushing technique, non-abrasive toothpaste, and a soft-bristled toothbrush. Be sure to floss once a day or after meals to remove any food particles from between the teeth. You can also use antibacterial mouthwash to keep the breath and gums fresh and free from bacteria. Keep your gums clean Healthy gums play a crucial role in overall oral health, which can help to maintain your dental implants. Good gum health keeps gum disease, gingivitis, and advanced gum disease like periodontitis at bay. It preserves the integrity of the artificial root systems of implant dentures and contributes to their long-term success. Regularly check for red, swollen, or irritated gums, and if you notice anything abnormal, especially near the implant site, contact your dentist. Visit your dentist for regular cleanings and check-ups Make it a habit to schedule twice-yearly dental cleanings and check-ups with your dentist. During routine dental cleanings, your dentist will remove plaque and tartar buildup that at-home brushing and flossing don’t address. They’ll also be able to get below the surface of the gums where your toothbrush can’t reach and polish the teeth to remove surface stains and create a smooth feel. During check-ups, the dentist will do a comprehensive oral exam, checking the mouth, cheeks, gums, tongue, and jaw to promote healthy functioning. Similarly, they’ll look at any dental devices like implants, crowns, and dentures and make sure everything is in order. Avoid hard or sticky foods Hard foods, like certain nuts, vegetables, or candies, can damage the teeth and put excessive pressure on implant dentures or damage artificial teeth. Chewy foods like gum, taffy, or tough meats can get stuck on or around the implants and cause them to shift out of place or even dislodge the artificial tooth entirely. Limit your intake of these kinds of foods, and chew slowly and carefully when you do eat them. Look for signs of infection Regularly check your implant dentures for signs of infection, like swelling, bleeding between the teeth or around the gums, or discharge at the implant site. If the area is unusually painful or tender, especially when chewing or speaking, visit your dentist right away to identify the cause and create a treatment plan. Wear a night guard Grinding the teeth, also called bruxism, can damage both natural and artificial teeth, causing wear and tear to the surface of the teeth and putting pressure on the root or artificial root system. A night guard can help minimize the impact of grinding, preserve your implant dentures, and protect the investment you made toward dental implant costs. It can also reduce stress on the jaw and jawbone and reduce gum recession. Check for broken parts Part of ongoing implant denture care is making sure the components of the implants are functioning properly and don’t cause damage to the mouth. If you notice broken parts or missing pieces on or around your implant dentures, contact your dentist right away. The quicker they can diagnose a problem, the quicker it can be resolved and lessen the risk of further damage. The bottom line If you have broken or missing teeth, dental implants can be a life-changing procedure. Implant dentures can restore your ability to chew and eat comfortably, speak clearly and confidently, and smile more often. By practicing good oral hygiene habits, visiting your dentist twice annually, and regularly checking your dental implants, you can extend and preserve their lifespan and make sure you’ve got a healthy, happy smile for years to come. press_release_title: How to Find the Right Wedding Planner for You
press_release_text: For couples planning a wedding, there’s no doubt that the phrase “it takes an army” rings true. From cake-tasting to creating the guest list—there can be a lot on your plate while planning your wedding. But with all these moving parts, one piece may be essential: finding the right wedding planner. A wedding planner that you and your future spouse trust might make all the difference when planning your special day. They’ll work closely with you on bringing your dream wedding to life, so you want to find someone who understands your vision. Here are a few tips on how to find the right wedding planner for you: Find the planner that can bring your vision to life Start by making a list of potential planners and do your research online—see reviews, ask for referrals from family and friends, and even review their portfolios. Once you’ve narrowed it down to a few options, reach out for one-on-one meetings with the Wedding Planners you’re considering. Discuss budgeting and payment plans during these meetings to ensure you are comfortable with the arrangement before committing. Determining what kind of atmosphere or style you want for your big day is crucial. Are you looking for a traditional wedding or something more modern? Do you want an intimate gathering or a big bash? Once you’ve decided on what type of event you’d like, research different planners specializing in that style. Check if they can work with your budget Budget is always one of the most important factors when choosing a wedding planner, as it can determine which services they provide and which vendors they work with. Before meeting with potential planners, decide how much money you’re willing to spend and ensure they can work within your budget constraints. Some planners may even be able to help negotiate discounts with certain vendors they work with frequently, so be sure to ask about any potential cost savings before deciding. Wedding loans are also available if you need help with your budget—your wedding planner may know about good loan options. Ask for recommendations Personal recommendations from friends and family can be invaluable when searching for a wedding planner. Not only can they tell you about their own positive experiences, but they may also warn you about which ones to avoid. Most reputable planners will have online reviews from past clients that can also give prospective customers an honest opinion about what it’s like working with them. Make sure you like them because you’ll be spending a while together Finally, don’t forget one of the most essential qualities of any good wedding planner—personality! When interviewing potential candidates, take some time to get to know them better by asking questions not just related directly to their services. More personal topics like interests or hobbies may help you determine if you like each other—you may find out that you have more in common than expected. Remember, this person will work very closely with you throughout your planning process, so choose someone you’re comfortable spending time with. The Bottom Line Choosing the right wedding planner for your special day comes down to two main factors—finding someone who understands your vision AND can work within your budget constraints. Having great chemistry between yourself and your wedding planner is no less important than the logistics. So, get acquainted before committing—after all, you may work closely with your planner throughout this journey! press_release_title: Aflac: Should Anyone Borrow Money from a Life Insurance Policy?
press_release_text: Permanent life insurance is usually more than a tool helping to offer lifelong financial protection. The cash value component helps offer policyholders a potential wealth-building source. Policyholders can use this cash value by borrowing from it. This can let them recoup some of the premiums paid, like with return of premium life insurance , but without losing lifelong coverage. However, as with any debt, policyholders may be cautious about whether getting a loan against their policy is the right move. This article will dive into the benefits of borrowing from a life insurance policy and explore several situations where a policy loan can benefit one financially. Benefits of borrowing from a life insurance policy Borrowing from life insurance can offer several benefits to a policyholder: No credit checks required: Life insurance loans don’t require credit checks, preventing a hard inquiry and helping those with lower credit scores get loans. 1 Low interest rates: Policy loans typically offer lower rates than traditional loans and credit cards, making them easier to afford. 2 No fixed repayment date: Policy loans have no fixed repayment schedule. 1 The borrower repays on their schedule. The policy stays active as long as the loan remains smaller than the cash value. Tax advantages available: Policy loans generally aren’t taxable unless the policy lapses. This offers a tax-efficient way to supplement one’s savings or income. 2 Four situations where borrowing from life insurance can make sense Understanding how to borrow against life insurance and its benefits can help the policyholder in several situations: 1. Refinancing and consolidating debt Refinancing typically involves paying off a loan or credit card with a new, lower-rate loan. Consolidating usually involves paying off multiple debts with one to help streamline debt management. Policyholders can do both by borrowing from their policies since rates can be more cost-effective. This can help save on interest and make tracking debt easier. 2. Covering emergencies Policy loans can help cover emergency costs at a lower interest rate than traditional loans or credit cards. 2 One can borrow quickly and spread out repayment since there’s no fixed repayment date. 1 Even if one has an emergency fund, a policy loan can help supplement it and reduce reliance on higher-interest debt. 3. Paying for education costs Education can be one of the most significant costs parents pay. A cash value loan can help cover some or all the cost. Interest rates may be on par with federal student loans and better than private loans. Plus, the repayment schedule helps parents spread repayment over a longer period. 4. Supplementing retirement Retirement accounts tend to have contribution limits or may not offer a wide range of investment choices. The life insurance cash value can offer an additional tax-advantaged way to help save for retirement. Once one retires, they can utilize their cash value with loans to supplement their other savings and assets. The bottom line Permanent life insurance can be an excellent financial vehicle beyond its financial protection. Borrowing from the policy can offer a quick loan at low rates with no credit check or fixed repayment date. So, these loans can help refinance and consolidate debt, cover emergencies, pay for education costs, and supplement retirement savings, among other situations. The earlier one gets a permanent life insurance policy, the more competitive their premiums and the longer they have to build cash value. Therefore, prospective policyholders should shop for policies today if they want to use one as an additional savings vehicle. Sources: 1 Bankrate – Borrowing against your life insurance policy. press_release_title: What to Consider When Financing a Collector Car
press_release_text: It can take years to save for an antique car. Applying for financing could help make that purchase possible and faster. There are many ways to finance a classic car, including a home equity loan, bank loan or personal loan. But, deciding on the right classic car loan option can be difficult, especially for those who are new to the collecting world. Here are six factors collectors should have on their radar when financing a classic car: 1. Credit Creditworthiness will be an important factor when financing a classic car. Collectors should check their credit scores to better understand their options. Then, they can take steps to improve their score, if necessary. In general, lenders may consider a higher credit score more favorable, but what qualifies as a “good” score will vary based on the credit score model and lender that uses it. A higher score may also help a collector access a lower interest rate for whatever type of loan is selected. 2. Down payment Car loans designed for classic cars through a traditional bank may require a down payment of 10% or more to qualify. Higher down payments often decrease long-term costs, though it can take more time and patience to save up to get that down payment. A personal loan could offer a classic car enthusiast another financing option if they cannot provide a down payment upfront or just want more flexibility. 3. Interest rate and loan term The loan’s interest rate and its term are the two biggest factors that determine the total cost of the loan. A lower interest rate with a shorter term can save the borrower the most money. But a shorter term may also mean a higher monthly payment, compared with the monthly payment for a longer-term loan. Considering different terms and lenders can help a collector balance the short- and long-term costs to make the best decision for their needs. 4. Loan-to-value ratio Auto lenders generally use the loan-to-value (LTV) ratio to determine if a loan makes sense. This ratio divides the total loan amount by the estimated car value and multiplies that figure by 100. Lower LTV ratios are generally better. Let’s say a collector applies for a $20,000 loan on a car valued at $18,000. The lender likely would not approve that loan because of the high LTV ratio (over 100%). However, a $12,000 loan for the same vehicle would have a much lower LTV ratio (around 67%). Increasing the down payment on a higher LTV car can help lower the ratio. That strategy may help a collector qualify for financing. 5. Car condition A collector car’s general condition can shape the purchase decision. For example, some collectors may prefer a high-quality car, even if it means a higher loan amount and waiting to find their ideal car. Online value assessment tools, such as the National Automobile Dealers Association and the JD Power price guide, can help determine a vehicle’s condition. And running a car’s Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) can provide context about a car’s repair and inspection history. 6. Long-term costs Beyond the loan, a collector should consider other financial obligations that impact the cost of their new car. For example, collector car owners need specialized insurance to get adequate coverage for their vehicle. Lenders often require proof of insurance before finalizing a loan. And classic car insurance policies may have requirements, such as use limitations and secure storage. Collector cars can require more expensive parts and maintenance to run smoothly and preserve value. Factoring in those costs can help avoid larger bills that may come with inconsistent maintenance. The bottom line Classic car loans can help a fast-track collector’s dream of owning their favorite vintage car. But, before applying for a loan, a collector should consider the upfront price, the car’s condition and long-term costs. That way, they can get both affordability and quality out of their “new” car. press_release_title: Should I Take Out a Home Equity Loan to Install a Pool?
press_release_text: A backyard pool can be a great addition to your home. It offers a fun place to relax, exercise and entertain family and friends. But installing a pool isn’t cheap. So, if you’re thinking about getting one, you might be wondering if a home equity loan or another type of pool loan is the right way to pay for it. Let’s take a closer look at what a home equity loan is, its benefits and whether it’s a smart choice for your situation. What is a home equity loan? A home equity loan allows you to borrow money based on the equity you have in your home. Equity is the difference between your home’s market value and what you owe on your mortgage. For example, if your home is worth $300,000 and you still owe $200,000, you have $100,000 in equity. Lenders typically allow you to borrow up to 80% of your home’s equity. A home equity loan works like a traditional loan. You get a lump sum of money upfront and repay it in fixed monthly payments over a set period, usually 5 to 15 years. These loans typically have lower interest rates (cost of borrowing) than credit cards or personal loans because the borrower’s home is used as collateral to secure the loan. One downside is the lender has the right to repossess the home if you don’t make payments. Consider how much a pool could cost Before deciding how to pay for a pool, it’s important to understand the costs. The price of a swimming pool varies depending on the size, materials and features you choose. Above-ground pools : $1,000 – $20,000 In-ground vinyl pools : $20,000 – $40,000 In-ground fiberglass pools : $25,000 – $60,000 In-ground concrete pools : $35,000 – $65,000 On top of the initial cost, you’ll also need to budget for ongoing maintenance, repairs and higher utility bills. Having a solid estimate of these costs could help you figure out what makes the most sense for your budget before you apply for a home equity loan. Pros of using a home equity loan for a pool Applying for a home equity loan to finance your pool has several advantages: Lower interest rate : Home equity loans usually have lower interest rates because the home acts as collateral, making this kind of loan a more affordable option. Fixed payments : You’ll have predictable monthly payments which could help with budgeting. Potential home value increase : A well-maintained pool could add value to your home making it more attractive to buyers in the future. Cons of using a home equity loan for a pool While a home equity loan has benefits, there are also risks to consider, including: Your home is collateral : If you fail to make payments, the lender can foreclose on your home. Long-term commitment : Since these loans have repayment terms of up to 15 years, you could be paying for your pool long after you stop using it. Closing costs : Home equity loans come with closing costs which can be 2% to 5% of the loan amount. Other pool financing options If you’re not sure about using a home equity loan, there are some other pool loans and financing options to consider: Personal loans : This option allows you to borrow a lump sum of money and repay in monthly installments. Depending on the lender, you can apply for a secured or unsecured loan. In many cases, the collateral used for a secured personal loan is an automobile. Home equity line of credit (HELOC) : Unlike a home equity loan, a HELOC is a revolving line of credit and works a lot like a credit card. You can borrow money as needed and only pay interest on what you use during the draw period. You’ll repay the interest and principal (original loan amount) during the repayment period. Cash-out refinance : A cash-out refinance lets you replace your existing mortgage with a larger one, giving you access to the extra funds — perfect for financing a new pool. While refinancing does involve fees, the bigger factor to watch is the interest rate and APR. Homeowners typically choose to refinance when interest rates are falling, not rising. Is a home equity loan the right choice for you? Deciding whether to use a home equity loan for a pool depends on your financial situation and long-term goals. Here are a few questions to ask yourself: Can I afford the monthly payments without straining my budget? Do I plan to stay in my home long enough to enjoy the pool and see a return on investment? Am I comfortable using my home as collateral for a loan in addition to my mortgage? Have I compared other financing options? If you have strong home equity, a stable income and a long-term plan to stay in your home, a home equity loan could be a smart way to finance your pool. However, if you’re unsure about taking on that form or any debt or plan to move soon, exploring other options may be a better choice. Consider all your options before you take the dip A pool can bring years of enjoyment but it’s important to carefully consider how to finance it. While a home equity loan possibly offers a low interest rate and fixed payments, it also comes with risks. Before making a decision, compare different pool loans and financing options and make sure the investment aligns with your financial goals. With the right planning, you could turn your backyard into an oasis. SPONSORED CONTENT Media Contact Information Name: Sonakshi Murze Email: [email protected] Job Title: Manager
